systemsMapSummary: The trial is a team product that begins as a single-player experience. A team lead signs up, works through a 7-step workspace-setup wizard alone, and creates a first project (54% do). But the product's value only appears once the team is inside it, and three things block that: nothing prompts an invite after the first project (71% never invite), imported cards from spreadsheets or Trello are hard to find again, and the trial is quiet in week one so there is no reason to return. Solo setup means no teammates; no teammates means no shared board (only 22% reach one); no shared board means the collaborative value never lands, and conversion sits at 6.0%.
headline: If we turned solo setup into a team invite at the first-project moment, we'd likely see activation move from 22% toward the target and conversion rise from 6.0% without discounting.

causeEffect.from: No invite prompt after first project

loops: Solo loop: solo setup -> no teammate -> no shared board -> no collaborative value -> no reason to invite -> stays solo.
Trust loop: lost imported cards -> lower trust -> lead won't show colleagues -> fewer teammates -> less shared usage.

comb.barrier: The 7-step wizard front-loads effort before any value; median time-to-first-project is 3 days.
comb.significance: Adds friction at the moment motivation is highest

comb.barrier: After migration, users can't find imported cards, so they doubt they set it up correctly.
There is no in-product prompt to invite a teammate after the first project is created.
Setup is a single-player experience; teammates are absent, so there is no social pull to collaborate.
Leads may not see why a shared board beats their spreadsheet until a teammate is in it.
Nothing makes returning in week one feel natural; the quiet trial builds no habit.

strongestBarriers.barrier: No invite prompt at the first-project moment, so setup ends solo
strongestBarriers.rationale: Highest impact and highly changeable — a defaults-and-friction problem: the absence of a prompt at the moment of peak intent is why 71% never invite. Adding it converts existing intent into a team the product can prove value to.

strongestBarriers.barrier: Lost imported cards erode trust right after migration
strongestBarriers.rationale: Trust is fragile at migration; a broken 'where did my work go?' moment (salience + loss aversion about migrated data) stops leads from showing colleagues.

strongestBarriers.barrier: Single-player setup removes any social proof to collaborate
strongestBarriers.rationale: Because teammates are absent, the descriptive norm inside the workspace is 'work alone', reinforcing the solo loop.

barrierNarratives.point: Prompt a teammate invite at the moment the first project is created
barrierNarratives.narrative: The intent to build a team is highest just after the first project exists, but nothing acts on it. Placing the invite at that moment removes friction rather than adding persuasion — the cheapest, most reversible lever.

barrierNarratives.point: Make imported cards from spreadsheets or Trello easy to find after migration
barrierNarratives.narrative: A lead who can't find migrated work assumes the tool failed and won't risk showing colleagues. Restoring visibility protects trust at the exact moment it is most brittle.

barrierNarratives.point: Give the team lead a reason to return within the first 48 hours
barrierNarratives.narrative: A quiet week one lets the trial go cold. A single, well-timed reason to return keeps the account warm long enough for the team to arrive.

gapLog.content: Week-one in-product engagement is not instrumented, so the 'quiet trial' barrier is inferred, not measured.
The 19%-vs-3% invite/no-invite gap is treated as directional; inviting may mark already-committed teams rather than cause conversion.
Confirm ownership of the 7-step workspace-setup wizard across Product and Support before changing it.
No data on how often imported cards are actually lost versus merely hard to find.

discoveryActivities: 5-8 contextual interviews with recent team leads at the first-project moment to confirm why setup ends solo.
A journey/friction audit of the 7-step workspace-setup wizard, timing each step to first value.
A support-ticket audit quantifying how often 'where did my imported cards go?' recurs and its resolution.
Instrument week-one in-product engagement so the 'quiet trial' barrier can be measured rather than assumed.
